newsitem.title: USA: Stampeder outlines post-Morgan deal outlook.
newsitem.headline: Stampeder outlines post-Morgan deal outlook.

text.p: Stampeder Exploration Ltd, close to closing a possible C$512 million buyout of Morgan Hydrocarbons Inc, would spend $300 million over six years for heavy oil exploration if the merger goes through, Stampeder's top executive told Reuters.

"We expect to spend to C$300 million or C$50 million a year over the next six years for heavy oil exploration," Stampeder president and chief executive Jeff Tonken said after speaking at the Herold's Pacesetters Energy Conference here.
Tonken said the combined company would likely add 75 million barrels of heavy crude reserves in five years.
The combined company would now have 94 million barrels of reserves, and 1.7 million net acres of undeveloped land, most of it in Saskatchewan, he said.
He also said the market capitalization of the combined company would be C$900 million, and cash flow per share would be C$1.50.
Regarding the likelihood of the deal going through, Tonken said he was very confident it would.
"We signed a friendly deal," he said. "The only thing that could stop it would be a third party intervention," Tonken said.
Morgan has agreed to pay a C$10 million termination fee if its shareholders accept a higher offer from a rival bidder.
-- Franklin Paul, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
